Attempts 1 Deliver 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington, Dec. 30, 1919 Mr. William Frank Sequim, Washington My dear Mr. Frank: If your girls live within reach of public schools, I cannot receive them at Cushman, but if they live too far to attend a public school I shall be glad to receive them. If you sign your children up to three years at School, the School will pay transportation, otherwise, you will be obliged to pay their transportation yourself. This will mean however, that the children will remain at school until they have finished their term. Inasmuch as Cushman closes next June, your children will be transferred to Chemawa. A request for transportation must come thru Mr. A. N. Taylor, teacher in Jamestown Day School, Dungeness, who must certify that the children have completed the work given at his school. Very truly yours, Superintendent. EHH:MG Copy to Mr. Taylor. RECORD OF PUPIL IN SCHOOL Record of Margaret Frank at [Name of school.] School. Reproduced at the National Archives at Seattle BRIEF. APPLICATION OF William Frank FOR THE ENROLLMENT OF Margaret Frank IN THE INDIAN SCHOOL AT Tacoma, Wash. POST-OFFICE ADDRESS OF APPLICANT: Sequim, Wash. Date of enrollment, July 6, 1920 Term of enrollment, Three (3) years. NAME OF PERSON ARRANGING FOR THE TRANSFER: Position, APPLICATION FOR ENROLLMENT IN A NONRESERVATION SCHOOL. (For a child not enrolled at an Agency.) For and in consideration of the United States assuming the care, education, and maintenance in the United States Indian School at Tacoma, Wyo., of Margaret Frank, F. I. 16, I, William Frank of Degayon, P. O., State of Wash., do hereby voluntarily consent and agree to her enrollment in said school for a period of three years, and also obligate and bind myself to abide by all the rules and regulations for Indian schools. I further say that the said child was born at Shoshonean Road, Dec. 5, 1903, that the father, William Frank, a [illegible] Indian of the Clallam Tribe located at Gishmanu Agency; that he left the tribe about [illegible]; that the mother, Sarah Frank, was [illegible] Indian of the Shokomish Tribe located at Cushenonu Agency, and that she talks about [illegible]; that the said child was born and reared in the United States, and now actually resides therein; and that he has attended the following schools:
NAME OF SCHOOL—PUBLIC GOVERNMENT, OR MISSION LOCATED AT— DATE OF ENROLLMENT. DATE OF DISCHARGE. CAUSE OF DISCHARGE. GRADE.
Public—Div. 3 V Washington Harbor School close 7th Dec.
Should the child be returned home for one of the vacation periods of this enrollment at my request I further agree to pay all expenses, including round-trip railroad fares, sleeping-car fares, meals, lodging, stage fares, telegraph and telephone messages, and other incidental expenses connected with the visit. I further agree that said pupil shall be returned to the Cushenonu school on or before the last day of the vacation leave of absence. I further agree to deposit with the superintendent of the school sufficient money to defray all expenses to be incurred, and should the child fail to return to school at such time as agreed upon, I, myself and the superintendent of the school, the amount of money remaining with the superintendent, necessary to the return transportation of the child so neglecting to return, shall be forfeited to the Government. This 6th day of June, 1920 Two witnesses: O. H. Keller A. M. Frank (Parent, guardian, or next of kin.) NOTE.—Every blank in this application must be properly filled out by the applicant, in his own handwriting, if possible. I hereby certify that on Jan. 6, 1920, I made a careful examination of the physical condition of Margaret Frank, the child named in the foregoing application, and found her to be in proper physical condition to attend school. I therefore recommend that the said child be enrolled in this school. This 6 day of Jan., 1920 Claude W. Kennedy School Physician. The law provides: "That no part of this appropriation, or any other appropriation provided for herein except appropriations made pursuant to treaties, shall be used to educate children of less than one-fourth Indian blood whose parents are citizens of the United States and of the State wherein they live and where there are adequate free-school facilities provided and the facilities of the Indian schools are needed for pupils of more than one-fourth Indian blood." EXTRACTS FROM SCHOOL RULES. If the facilities of a school are not needed as provided in the above paragraph, children showing any Indian blood, whose parents live on an Indian reservation, and who if debarred from Government schools could not obtain an education, may be enrolled in the day and boarding schools of their reservation; these children, however, may not be transferred to nonreservation schools without special permission from the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Before enrolling a pupil superintendents must satisfy themselves whether he has left any other school without permission and whether he has been expelled for cause from any other school. A pupil who has been expelled for cause from any Indian school may be reenrolled in any Indian school only with permission of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Attention is invited to Circulars Nos. 1039 and 1044, which must be observed. "The Secretary of the Interior may in his discretion withhold rations, clothing, and other annuities from Indian parents or guardians who refuse or neglect to send or keep their children of proper school age in some school during a reasonable portion of each year." (27 Stat. L., 635. See 2 Dec. Comp., 308.)
